package.name: Log
package.description: Structured logging: levels, typed fields, text and JSON-lines records, a process-wide log for every thread, and log files that rotate by size

modules.name: Field
modules.header: The structured part of a record: named values beside its message.

modules.name: Global
modules.header:
The process-wide log: records written to standard error, from any thread.
Its settings are module variables read and written atomically, and a lock is held only for the one write of a
finished record, so threads build their records at the same time and never interleave them.

modules.name: Level
modules.header: How severe a record is, and the least severe level a build keeps.

modules.name: Logger
modules.header: A logger that writes records to a stream of its own.

modules.name: Record
modules.header:
Writing a record as one line of text or of JSON.
A record is built whole in memory and handed to its destination in one write, so records from different loggers,
or from the process-wide functions on different threads, never interleave within a line. A message or value that
holds a line break or another control character has it escaped, so one record is always one line.

modules.name: Rotation
modules.header:
A log file that is moved aside for a fresh one before it grows past a size, keeping a few of the older files.
The file is a `Writer`, so a `Logger` writes to it like any other destination; `RotatingFile::Stream` is the
stored form a `Logger` keeps, as `File::Stream` is for a plain file.

doc.summary:
The least severe level this build keeps, from the `LogLevel` build define: `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn` or
`error`, and `trace` when it is not defined.
doc.markdown:
The least severe level this build keeps, from the `LogLevel` build define: `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn` or
`error`, and `trace` when it is not defined. A record below it is dropped before anything about it is done,
whatever level a logger is set to, so a release build can leave out its tracing entirely.

doc.summary: Writes records at or above a level to a stream, each as one write.
doc.markdown:
Writes records at or above a level to a stream, each as one write. Not copied.
A logging call never fails: the first failure to write is kept for `Failure` to report, and the records after it
are still attempted. A logger is used by one thread at a time; the process-wide functions such as `Info` are the
ones to share between threads.

doc.summary: A log file that starts afresh before a write would take it past a size.
doc.markdown:
A log file that starts afresh before a write would take it past a size.
The current file keeps the path it was opened at. Moving it aside renames it to `path.1`, after renaming an
older `path.1` to `path.2` and so on up to `path.<keep>`, whose previous contents are replaced; with `keep` zero
the current file is emptied instead. The file is moved aside only before a write, never during one, and a
`Logger` hands each record over in one write, so a record never spans two files: one larger than the limit goes
whole into a file of its own.
Move-only: the file closes exactly once, through `Close` or the destructor.

doc.summary: Moves the current file aside now and starts an empty one, whatever its size.
doc.markdown:
Moves the current file aside now and starts an empty one, whatever its size.
The file is closed first, because Windows renames no open file. A failure leaves the current file closed,
and every later write fails with `InvalidHandle` until a rotation succeeds.
doc.returns: success when an empty current file is open
